H5305.name: Naphish
H5305.desc: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
H5305.brief: Son of Ishmael, defeated by Reubenites, Gadites, and Manassites.
H5305.short: Naphish, a son of Ishmael, was among the Hagrite tribes defeated by the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

H5321G.name: Naphtali
H5321G.desc: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
H5321G.brief: Son of Jacob, founder of the tribe of Naphtali.
H5321G.short: Naphtali, the sixth son of Jacob and second son of Bilhah, was the founder of the Israelite tribe that bore his name.

H5320.name: Naphtuhim
H5320.brief: Descendants of Mizraim, son of Ham
H5320.short: The Naphtuhim were descendants of Mizraim, son of Ham, who settled in northern Egypt.

H5353G.name: Nekoda
H5353G.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H5353G.brief: A family of temple servants who returned from exile.
H5353G.short: The descendants of Nekoda were among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

H5353H.name: Nekoda
H5353H.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H5353H.brief: Family excluded from the priesthood after the Exile.
H5353H.short: The descendants of Nekoda were among those who could not prove their priestly lineage after returning from the Babylonian exile.

H5303.name: Nephilim
H5303.brief: Mysterious giants mentioned in the pre-flood and post-flood eras.
H5303.short: The Nephilim were a race of giants mentioned in the context of the sons of God marrying human women before the flood and later encountered by the Israelite spies in Canaan.

H5300.name: Nephushesim
H5300.brief: Family of temple servants who returned from exile.
H5300.short: The Nephushesim (or Nephisim) were a family of temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

H5369G.name: Ner
H5369G.desc: Saul's uncle living at the time of United Monarchy
H5369G.brief: Father of Abner, King Saul's commander.
H5369G.short: Ner was the father of Abner, the commander of King Saul's army, and a member of Saul's family.

H5371H.name: Nergal-sar-ezer
H5371H.desc: Babylonian official living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5371H.brief: Future Babylonian king at Jerusalem's fall
H5371H.short: Nergal-sar-ezer was a Babylonian official present at the capture of Jerusalem in 587 BC and probably became king Neriglissar.

H5371G.name: Nergal-sar-ezer
H5371G.desc: Babylonian official of Samgar living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5371G.short: Nergal-sar-ezer the Rab-mag was a Babylonian official present at the capture of Jerusalem in 587 BC.

H5374.name: Neriah
H5374.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5374.short: Neriah was the father of Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe.

H5335.name: Neziah
H5335.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H5335.short: Neziah was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.

H5316G.name: Naphath
H5316G.brief: A region in Issachar with Manassite towns
H5316G.short: Naphath was a region in Issachar that contained towns belonging to the tribe of Manasseh.

H5318.name: Nephtoah
H5318.brief: A spring on the border of Judah and Benjamin
H5318.short: Nephtoah was a spring that served as a boundary marker between the territories of Judah and Benjamin.

H5334.name: Nezib
H5334.brief: A town in the Judean lowlands
H5334.short: Nezib was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the lowland region.

H5370.name: Nergal
H5370.brief: A Mesopotamian god worshipped by the Assyrians
H5370.short: Nergal, mentioned in <ref="2Ki.17.30">2Ki.17.30</ref>, was a Mesopotamian god of war, pestilence, and the underworld, worshipped by the men of Cuth who were brought to Samaria by the Assyrians.
